channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov Meets Residents of Issyk-Kul Region
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov met with residents of Karakol city and Tup and Ak-Suu districts in the Issyk-Kul region. Citizens raised issues concerning socio-economic development and pressing problems, including youth education, housing, and tourism. Appeals also covered child support, agricultural producer support, and law enforcement activities.

item.title: Ucell Expands 5G Network to All Regional Centers in Uzbekistan
item.description: Ucell has extended its 5G network to all regional centers across Uzbekistan, including major cities in the Fergana Valley and Samarkand region. The company, a pioneer in 5G deployment in the country, continues to broaden its high-speed coverage, maintaining its position as Uzbekistan's fastest mobile network operator.

item.title: Kazakh Citizen's Russian Company Declared Bankrupt, Debts Exceeding 105 Million Rubles for Sale
item.description: A Russian agricultural company owned by a Kazakh citizen, 'Ptitsеkompleks-Agro,' has gone bankrupt. The rights to claim debts totaling over 105.5 million rubles are now up for auction. The company, registered in Crimea, was declared bankrupt in May 2019, with the bankruptcy proceedings ongoing.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Gas Imports Surge by 50% from Russia and Turkmenistan
item.description: Uzbekistan has seen a 50% increase in its natural gas imports, drawing supplies from both Russia and Turkmenistan. This significant rise in energy imports highlights the country's growing demand and reliance on external sources for its energy needs.

item.title: Uzbekistan Establishes Special Agency to Oversee Citizen and Company Bankruptcies
item.description: Uzbekistan has approved regulations for a new Agency for Insolvency Affairs under the Ministry of Justice. This agency will oversee bankruptcy procedures for individuals and organizations, coordinate state bodies, and digitize the process. It aims to streamline procedures and reduce bureaucracy.

item.title: Kazakhstan Education Community Holds Congress in Turkistan to Discuss Key Issues
item.description: The Republican Congress of the Kazakhstan Continuous Education Community, themed 'Voice of the Sector – Strength of the Community,' convened in Turkistan. Representatives from government, business, and professional communities discussed pressing issues in education. The association, accredited by 'Atameken,' aims to improve the private preschool education sector.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Third Nuclear Power Plant Site on Tobol River
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering building its third nuclear power plant on the banks of the Tobol River in the Kostanay region, according to Almasadam Satkaliev, chairman of the Atomic Energy Agency. The agency is evaluating several potential locations, including sites near the Kurchatov polygon and the Caspian Sea, as well as a proposal for the Tobol River area. The Tobol River site offers sufficient water for cooling future reactors.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Warns of Politically Motivated Ethnic Unrest Ahead of Election
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov warned that politicians are attempting to provoke violence between ethnic Kyrgyz and Uzbeks to disrupt the upcoming presidential election. He did not provide evidence or identify those involved. Japarov's warning comes amid increased restrictions on opposition and independent media, raising concerns about political opponents being framed as national security threats.

item.title: Rustam Sakiev Appointed General Director of Kyrgyzstan's National Electric Grid
item.description: The Board of Directors of the National Electric Network of Kyrgyzstan (NESK) has appointed Rustam Sakiev as its new General Director. Sakiev, who has worked in the energy sector since 2011, previously led the Naryn electric grid enterprise. His appointment was announced by the Deputy Minister of Energy, who outlined priorities including network modernization and reliable supply.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans 15 MW Floating Solar Plant to Combat Energy Shortages
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to construct a 15 MW floating solar power plant on HPP-5 reservoir near Bishkek to reduce reliance on electricity imports. The country expects to import 4.1 billion kWh in 2026. The Asian Development Bank is proposing $20 million in financing for the project, which aims to establish a model for future floating solar installations.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank Orders Banks to Cancel Illegal Loan Charges
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank has mandated commercial banks to conduct internal audits of loans with existing court enforcement orders. Banks must cancel illegally accrued interest, fines, and penalties, and return collected sums to borrowers. The audit must be completed by December 10, 2026, with reports due by December 25, 2026.

item.title: Manas Airport Investigates Aircraft After Bomb Threat Report
item.description: An S7 Airlines plane arriving from Novosibirsk at Manas International Airport in Bishkek is being investigated following a report of a potential explosive device on board. The aircraft landed safely with 158 passengers, who were evacuated. The plane was moved to a secure location for inspection by canine units.

item.title: Kazakhstan: 12 former prison staff receive sentences for prisoner abuse
item.description: A court in Kazakhstan's Akmola region sentenced 12 former prison employees to two years of restricted freedom for exceeding their authority in a case involving the beating of inmates, including activist Timur Danebaev. Nine received one year after amnesty, while three were released due to time served. They are also banned from law enforcement roles for three years.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan seeks climate finance at COP31, proposes global center for mountains
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Prime Minister requested simplified access to climate financing for mountainous countries at COP31, proposing a Global Center for Mountain Resilience. The country also secured $30 million in preferential financing from the ARISE program for water and agriculture resilience. Kyrgyzstan contributed $10 million to a trust fund for Issyk-Kul lake.

item.title: International tribunal rejects Turkish investors' claims against Uzbekistan
item.description: An international arbitration tribunal at the ICSID has rejected all claims filed by Turkish citizen Mehmet Zeki Obuz and others against Uzbekistan. The ruling concluded a five-year legal dispute related to the food industry. Uzbekistan's interests were represented by the Ministry of Justice and an international law firm.

item.title: Uzbekistan fugitive wanted for drug crimes apprehended in Russia
item.description: A citizen of Uzbekistan, wanted internationally for drug trafficking and other serious crimes, has been arrested in Russia's Khanty-Mansiysk region. The man was found working as a repairman. Authorities are currently processing his extradition to Uzbekistan. The Uzbek Interior Ministry expressed gratitude to Russian law enforcement for their professionalism in locating the fugitive.

item.title: First Islamic bank in Kazakhstan receives operating license
item.description: Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank (ADCB) has obtained its license to operate as the first Islamic bank in Kazakhstan. The license was presented during a financial congress, allowing the bank to offer both conventional and Islamic financial products. This marks a significant step in developing Islamic finance in the country.

item.title: Kazakhstan to freeze some uranium deposits for future nuclear power plants
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to freeze some uranium deposits to secure raw materials for its future nuclear power plants for their entire operational lifespan. The national reserve aims to accumulate at least 150,000 tons of uranium. This strategic move ensures a century's supply of uranium for the country's nuclear energy needs.

item.title: Tashkent to Host New SCO Center for Counter-Terrorism and Cyber Threats
item.description: A new universal Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) center focused on combating terrorism, extremism, and cyber threats will be established in Tashkent. It will be based on the existing regional anti-terrorist structure and will coordinate efforts among member states' law enforcement and intelligence agencies. A branch in Bishkek will focus on transnational organized crime.

item.title: Tajikistan to Receive €72.25 Million for Mountain Ecosystem Restoration
item.description: Tajikistan will receive €72.25 million for land restoration, mountain ecosystem recovery, and climate change adaptation in agriculture under the regional CLiCA program. The Green Climate Fund approved a €264.4 million budget for the seven-year initiative, with Uzbekistan also receiving significant funding.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Transfer Pension Assets in Government Bonds to Private Managers
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Bank plans to transfer a portion of pension assets invested in government securities to private management companies. This move aims to create a pool of both domestic and external managers, similar to the current practice for foreign financial instruments.

item.title: Tajikistan Raises Teacher Salaries Significantly, Yet Shortages Persist
item.description: Tajikistan has implemented substantial pay raises for teachers, increasing base salaries by a combined 62.5% between September 2025 and September 2026. Despite these increases, which brought average monthly salaries above the national average, schools continue to face shortages in key subjects.

item.title: COP31 Discusses Future of Nuclear Energy, Youth Role
item.description: At COP31 in Antalya, "World Nuclear Days" focused on training young specialists, developing human resources, and international cooperation for tripling global nuclear capacity by 2050. Rosatom Director General Alexey Likhachev emphasized the importance of youth in shaping the future of the industry and attracting talent.

item.title: Kazakhstan-China Rail Freight Volume Increases by 2.4 Million Tons
item.description: The volume of rail freight transportation between Kazakhstan and China has increased by 2.4 million tons. This growth highlights strengthening trade ties and logistical cooperation between the two neighboring countries.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Unified Early Warning System and Climate Financing for Central Asia
item.description: Uzbekistan has proposed a new framework for climate cooperation in Central Asia, calling for unified early warning systems, green technologies, and new financing mechanisms to combat growing environmental threats. President Mirziyoyev presented a three-part model for regional climate integration, addressing melting glaciers, water scarcity, and drought.

item.title: Expert: Legally Impossible to Dissolve Samruk-Kazyna Sovereign Wealth Fund
item.description: An expert states that legally dissolving the Samruk-Kazyna sovereign wealth fund is impossible due to its extensive financial obligations, including billions of dollars in loans, guarantees, and bonds. The fund manages strategic national assets and is crucial for international partnerships.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Presidential Race: 11 Candidates Emerge for January 2027 Election
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has announced an initial list of 11 candidates vying for the presidency in the election scheduled for January 27, 2027. The candidates include the incumbent president, former lawmakers, ex-heads of security agencies, businessmen, and a former CEC chairman. All are running as independents.

item.title: Expert warns of potential provocations ahead of Kyrgyzstan's elections
item.description: Political scientist Sheradil Baktygulov urges Kyrgyz citizens to take seriously the president's warning about potential unrest during the upcoming elections. He notes that provocations, driven by personal grudges or foreign influence, are common during election campaigns. Citizens are advised to be vigilant and assist authorities in identifying destructive actions.

item.title: Uzbekistan Business Ombudsman addresses entrepreneurial barriers
item.description: Uzbekistan's Business Ombudsman, Abdumannop Buriev, held a personal meeting with entrepreneurs to discuss and resolve issues hindering business activities. Key concerns included legal disputes, property rights, and bureaucratic obstacles in obtaining permits. The Ombudsman's office is committed to creating a favorable business environment.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Four former Tashkent court officials sentenced for lenient sentencing of Akmal Shukurov
item.description: A court in Tashkent region has sentenced four former judicial officials, including a deputy chief judge, for their role in leniently sentencing Akmal Shukurov. One received four years in prison, while three others received four years of restricted freedom.

item.title: Kazakhstan President's Address Outlines Initiatives to Improve Welfare in Mangystau Region
item.description: Working groups are explaining President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's address, 'Urgent Tasks of Kazakhstan in a New Historical Era,' to residents and work collectives in the Mangystau region. The address emphasizes political reforms and improving the quality of life, including accessible healthcare.

item.title: Kazakhstan's first nuclear power plant construction may begin in 2027
item.description: Construction of Kazakhstan's first nuclear power plant, "Balkhash," could commence in 2027, pending necessary licenses and legal compliance. An intergovernmental agreement and EPC contract with Russia have been signed, with further appendices under negotiation. The agency head stated Rosatom and Kazakh partners could begin construction in 2027.

item.title: Former deputy chairman and judges of Tashkent court sentenced for leniency in Akmal Shukurov case
item.description: A former deputy chairman of the Tashkent City Court and three former judges have been sentenced for issuing an unfair decision. The ex-deputy chairman received a 4-year prison sentence for negligence and interference in justice. The three former judges received 4-year suspended sentences for issuing an unfair decision.

item.title: European Leaders Assert Continent's Security Architecture is Self-Determined
item.description: European leaders, including France's Macron and Germany's Merz, stated that Europe will define its own security architecture, rejecting Russia's proposals. They view Russia's stance as a tactic to distract from the war in Ukraine and reassert global power. High-level representatives from France, Germany, the UK, Italy, the EU, and NATO met in Abu Dhabi but did not engage with the Russian delegation.

item.title: Fitch Assigns Karakalpakstan BB- Credit Rating with Stable Outlook
item.description: Fitch Ratings has assigned Uzbekistan's Republic of Karakalpakstan a long-term credit rating of BB- with a stable outlook. The rating cited Karakalpakstan’s reliance on central government transfers and limited revenue-raising powers.

item.title: IMF Recommends Central Asian Nations Tighten Monetary Policy Amid Inflation Risks
item.description: The IMF advises Central Asian countries to tighten monetary policy as a primary defense against inflation risks, which are projected to be higher than initially estimated. While inflation is slowing in Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan due to tighter policies, it remains above targets in most other regional nations, posing a significant concern for the fund.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Solidcore Resources to Explore Precious Metals in Tajikistan
item.description: Kazakhstan-based Solidcore Resources has signed an agreement with Tajikistan's Main Department of Geology to explore for precious metals and polymetallic ores. The memorandum was signed following talks between the presidents of Kazakhstan and Tajikistan. Solidcore Tajikistan will identify potential projects, with implementation and financing to be agreed upon separately. Tajikistan's gold production has grown significantly, with Chinese companies dominating the sector.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Beeline Owners in Talks to Establish a Bank
item.description: The owners of Kazakhstan's telecom operator Beeline, the Veon group, are in technical consultations with the regulator regarding the creation of a bank in Kazakhstan. Veon intends to enter the Kazakh market with a digital bank by the end of 2027, aiming to compete with major financial groups. The company is discussing various forms of market representation with the regulator.

item.title: Company Fined 200,000 Som for Improper Drainage System Construction in Talas
item.description: The state-owned enterprise "Batken Mobile Mechanization Unit" has been fined 200,000 som for violating construction norms during the installation of a closed drainage system on Tagaybaev Street in Talas. The Ministry of Construction reported that the inspection by the State Architecture-Construction Control Department found non-compliance with urban planning documents and technical regulations.

item.title: Uzbekistan Considers Establishing Media Ombudsman to Protect Journalists
item.description: Uzbekistan is exploring the creation of an independent media ombudsman to safeguard the rights of journalists and media professionals. This initiative is part of a plan to improve the country's ranking in Reporters Without Borders' press freedom index. The plan also includes an open electronic registry of cases against journalists.
